extracted.intended_audience: SNSF programme managers, policymakers, evaluators, Ambizione applicants/grantees and researchers interested in research funding design
extracted.subtask_description: Qualitative case studies and survey instrument used to evaluate the Swiss National Science Foundation's Ambizione funding scheme, focusing on grantee experiences with eligibility requirements, funding amount and duration, host-institute relations, career impact and suggested improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific independence / ability to lead own lab
rubrics_metrics.description: Ambizione allowed grantees to 'officially' work independently, lead their own junior group and mentor students; enabled grantees to make a name for themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: first-author publications attributed to independence; employment of doctoral students provided leadership experience; respondents frequently stated that Ambizione made independent research possible in ways a regular postdoc would not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant resources sufficiency for project completion
rubrics_metrics.description: The extent to which the Ambizione grant provided the necessary funds and equipment to realise the proposed project (e.g. 'He could not have afforded the measuring instrument').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrations: grantees sometimes needed host-institute co-funding for expensive equipment; some said they 'could not have conducted the project to the same extent without Ambizione'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of funding (three years)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the standard three-year funding period is sufficient to complete projects (e.g. 'three years ... can be too short for PhD students to finish their project').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples/suggestions: some grantees recommended four years; extensions were sometimes granted and considered important to enable career transitions or finish work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget allocation flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Flexibility to change the allocation of budget items during the funding period ('would have preferred to have a little more flexibility in allocating the budget').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeated suggestion to allow reallocation once the project is underway; several grantees noted the difficulty of planning detailed budgets early on and requested easier reallocation procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and appropriateness of funding requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: How clear, fair and appropriate the eligibility and mobility requirements are (e.g. 'The funding requirements were always clear' vs mobility being 'a prerequisite' but also 'a problem').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observations: some found mobility requirements adequate for Ambizione's goal to attract returnees; others noted mobility can disadvantage those with family duties; early regulations were sometimes open to contradictory interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation process: eligibility vs proposal quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether evaluation is based solely on meeting funding requirements or also on the scientific quality of the proposal ('evaluation of applications is not based exclusively on the funding requirements but also on the actual proposal').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implication: selection considers both eligibility and merit; applicants should ensure strong proposals in addition to meeting formal criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host institute support and integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which the host institute provides scientific, financial and administrative support (e.g. financing instruments, doctoral students, office space, administrative secretaries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: host institutes sometimes co-funded equipment or a doctoral student; good integration included participation in institute life, help with admin tasks, access to infrastructure; problems included misclassification by HR or unclear expectations about teaching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to and quality of infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether host institute infrastructure meets the project's needs ('the institute’s infrastructure ... which he evaluated as good').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grantees chose host institutes partly for specialised infrastructure; lack of suitable national infrastructure was cited as reason mobility within Switzerland may be counterproductive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to hire doctoral students/postdocs/technical staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether Ambizione funds can be used to employ doctoral students, postdocs or technicians (some grantees 'could not hire a doctoral student using his Ambizione grant').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SNSF later implemented the possibility to hire doctoral students; examples: where host institutes co-funded student help, projects progressed better; hiring staff increased attractiveness on the job market.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on concurrent funding/applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules that prevent grantees from applying for other project funding while holding an Ambizione grant ('Ambizione grantees cannot apply for project funding at the same time').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some grantees criticised this restriction and would have preferred the possibility to apply concurrently for other funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support and responsiveness of SNSF staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality and speed of administrative support from SNSF ('helpful, quick, competent and close to the grantees'; 'could call the responsible staff anytime').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grantees generally praised SNSF staff; some suggested more proactive coaching (e.g. job application coaching) and clearer guidance on annual reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of reporting requirements (annual reports)
rubrics_metrics.description: How clear the SNSF's rules are concerning reporting obligations ('requirements regarding the annual reports were not completely clear').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggestion: SNSF should provide additional assistance and clearer instructions for annual reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career impact / stepping-stone effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which Ambizione acts as a stepping stone to permanent positions, SNSF professorships, ERC grants or other career advancement ('Ambizione was one of the reasons ... given a permanent position earlier').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: helped return to Switzerland, boosted independence, improved competitiveness on the job market, helped obtain professorships and ERC funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution to national attractiveness and researcher retention
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether Ambizione helps position Switzerland as an attractive science location and retain or attract researchers ('helps to position Switzerland as an attractive science location' and 'can make researchers stay in the Swiss scientific community longer').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grantees saw Ambizione as encouraging returnees and retaining talent; some noted it may not attract more promising researchers but can prolong stays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity and gender considerations (equal funding)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether Ambizione promotes equal funding opportunities for women and those with family duties ('equal funding of women is generally not achieved').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested remedy: implement shared funding/job-sharing models where two researchers share budget and time to improve equality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobility requirement fairness (international and internal mobility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriateness of mobility requirements both for international return and mobility within Switzerland ('mobility within Switzerland requested by the SNSF makes sense?' vs mobility as prerequisite).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some argued mobility is essential for career development; others said internal mobility within a small country can be counterproductive when specialised infrastructure exists in one place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and complexity of career transition support
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability of coaching and support for job applications and career transitions during or after the grant ('would have appreciated coaching ... in applying for jobs').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grantees reported high time pressure near grant end due to job applications; suggested SNSF provide coaching or guidance on job application processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative effort and satisfaction with application procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent satisfaction with information/advice, administrative effort, submission requirements, and time to decision (survey items asking respondents to rate these aspects).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey response options included Very satisfied / Rather satisfied / Rather unsatisfied / Not at all satisfied / Not applicable; these are explicit metrics for process evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motives for applying (scheme attractiveness features)
rubrics_metrics.description: Motives such as option of returning to Swiss science community, developing one's own research focuses, studying new research questions, and reputation of the scheme (survey items listed as motives).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey asked grantees to rate these motives from 'Very significant' to 'Completely insignificant'; scheme design should consider these attractiveness factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host-institute HR/administrative compatibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarity and correctness of HR classification and administrative treatment at host institutions (example: misassignment to technical/administrative staff instead of research collaborator).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggestion: SNSF or an independent office could help troubleshoot conflicts or misunderstandings between host institutions and grantees about rights and duties (teaching obligations, classification).

rubrics_metrics.name: Networking and alumni/community support
rubrics_metrics.description: Importance of networking, exchange of information among grantees and access to alumni networks ('networking and the exchange of information ... is very important'; 'participates in the SNSF alumni network').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grantees acted as advisors to applicants; SNSF could facilitate networks and peer support to increase scheme benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to combine Ambizione with teaching and building reputation
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether grantees can (or choose to) teach during their Ambizione period and how teaching affects later career opportunities ('did not teach ... which later kept him from obtaining a position where teaching experience was required').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trade-off: teaching can aid later professorship applications and local visibility; standalone positions may make network-building harder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory stability and early-stage ambiguity
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which rules and regulations are stable and clear, noting that early grantees experienced contradictory interpretation ('regulations were not yet fully elaborated and thus open to some contradictory interpretation').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implication: clear, stable guidelines reduce administrative friction; early-adopter grantees may face more uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to reallocate funding mid-project and ease of budget planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical difficulties in preparing a budget 'at a point in time when grantees often do not know how to do this' and desire for regulations to 'allow for more flexibility' to change budget allocations during the funding period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeated feedback: make reallocation easier, allow adjustments as project details become clearer.
